text: Swimming relies on a synchronized action of limbs that ensures grace and propulsion. Forward motion originates from the kick; this precise leg movement pushes the body ahead. Once momentum builds, the arms enter their phase, drawing the swimmer through the fluid. Air management concludes the sequence. The head tilts to allow inhalation, followed by exhalation to purge carbon dioxide. Success depends on integrating these three components—kicking, paddling, and breathing. This integration produces efficient and graceful swimming.
